/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A variety of groups is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images
and (unrestricted) direct products; equivalently, it is the class of all groups satisfying
some set of laws. The varieties of groups, ordered by inclusion, form a complete lattice.
By a classical theorem (see H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1), the map sending a
variety $\mathfrak{V}$ to the subgroup $\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty)$ of all laws of $\mathfrak{V}$
is an anti-isomorphism from the lattice of all varieties of groups onto the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of the free group $F_\infty$ of countably infinite rank. We therefore
realise the lattice of all varieties of groups as the order dual of the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ`. This also avoids the set-theoretic issues involved in
working with classes of groups.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete 37,
  Springer, 1967.
-/

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.27».fullyInvariantSubgroup
justification.why_needed: Bundles the fully invariant subgroups of a group as a `CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G)` (with proofs of closure under sSup and sInf), giving the carrier type of the lattice of varieties its complete lattice structure; analogue of Mathlib's `fullyInvariantSubmodule`.

blocks.name: fullyInvariantSubgroup
blocks.text:
variable (G) in
/-- The fully invariant subgroups of a group `G` form a complete sublattice of the lattice of
subgroups of `G`. -/
def fullyInvariantSubgroup : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G) :=
  .mk' {H : Subgroup G | IsFullyInvariant H}
    (fun _s hs f => by
      rw [(Subgroup.gc_map_comap f).l_sSup]
      exact iSup₂_le fun H hH => (hs hH f).trans (le_sSup hH))
    fun _s hs f => le_sInf fun H hH => (Subgroup.map_mono (sInf_le hH)).trans (hs hH f)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_fullyInvariantSubgroup_iff {H : Subgroup G} :
    H ∈ fullyInvariantSubgroup G ↔ IsFullyInvariant H := Iff.rfl

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question: the Prop is that there exists a lattice automorphism (order-preserving bijection, hence preserving meets and joins) of the complete lattice of all varieties of groups (ordered by inclusion; equivalently, anti-isomorphic to the lattice of fully invariant subgroups of the free group of countably infinite rank) which is not the identity — one must take care to define varieties as classes closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and (unrestricted) direct products, or via laws, and to handle universe issues by working with the set of verbal/fully invariant subgroups of a countably generated free group rather than a class of groups.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ e : L ≃o L, e ≠ OrderIso.refl _`; they differ only in the model L. Seven use the fully invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ` (the standard Neumann anti-isomorphism 𝔙 ↦ 𝔙(F_∞); in F_∞ fully invariant = verbal, so this is exactly the set of varieties with reversed inclusion), c04 defines varieties directly as S/H/P-closed classes of groups in `Type` (also faithful by Birkhoff's theorem inside `Type`, but relies on a universe argument). Order automorphisms of a lattice are exactly lattice automorphisms, and I verified in Lean that (i) `e ≠ OrderIso.refl` ⟺ `∃ x, e x ≠ x`, and (ii) non-identity automorphisms of L and of Lᵒᵈ correspond bijectively, so every candidate is equivalent. c01 was chosen because it adds `ᵒᵈ` so its type is literally order-isomorphic (not merely anti-isomorphic) to the lattice of varieties ordered by inclusion, builds the lattice as a `CompleteSublattice` with sorry-free closure proofs, includes API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions, has a clear docstring, and compiles with only the sorry warning. Only edit: added the H. Neumann reference to the module docstring.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.27

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

A variety of groups is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images
and (unrestricted) direct products; equivalently, it is the class of all groups satisfying
some set of laws. The varieties of groups, ordered by inclusion, form a complete lattice.
By a classical theorem (see H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Chapter 1), the map sending a
variety $\mathfrak{V}$ to the subgroup $\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty)$ of all laws of $\mathfrak{V}$
is an anti-isomorphism from the lattice of all varieties of groups onto the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of the free group $F_\infty$ of countably infinite rank. We therefore
realise the lattice of all varieties of groups as the order dual of the lattice of fully
invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ`. This also avoids the set-theoretic issues involved in
working with classes of groups.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete 37,
  Springer, 1967.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.27»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup `H` of a group `G` is *fully invariant* if it is mapped into itself by every
endomorphism of `G`. -/
def IsFullyInvariant (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : G →* G, H.map f ≤ H

/-- The trivial subgroup is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_bot : IsFullyInvariant (⊥ : Subgroup G) := fun f => by
  simp

/-- The whole group is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_top : IsFullyInvariant (⊤ : Subgroup G) := fun _ => le_top

/-- The commutator subgroup is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFullyInvariant_commutator : IsFullyInvariant (commutator G) := fun f => by
  rw [commutator_def, Subgroup.map_commutator]
  exact Subgroup.commutator_mono le_top le_top

/-- A fully invariant subgroup is characteristic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFullyInvariant.characteristic {H : Subgroup G} (hH : IsFullyInvariant H) :
    H.Characteristic := by
  rw [Subgroup.characteristic_iff_map_le]
  exact fun φ => hH φ.toMonoidHom

variable (G) in
/-- The fully invariant subgroups of a group `G` form a complete sublattice of the lattice of
subgroups of `G`. -/
def fullyInvariantSubgroup : CompleteSublattice (Subgroup G) :=
  .mk' {H : Subgroup G | IsFullyInvariant H}
    (fun _s hs f => by
      rw [(Subgroup.gc_map_comap f).l_sSup]
      exact iSup₂_le fun H hH => (hs hH f).trans (le_sSup hH))
    fun _s hs f => le_sInf fun H hH => (Subgroup.map_mono (sInf_le hH)).trans (hs hH f)

/-- Membership in `fullyInvariantSubgroup G` is full invariance. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_fullyInvariantSubgroup_iff {H : Subgroup G} :
    H ∈ fullyInvariantSubgroup G ↔ IsFullyInvariant H := Iff.rfl

/-- The lattice of all varieties of groups (ordered by inclusion), realised as the order dual of
the lattice of fully invariant subgroups (ordered by inclusion) of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ`
of countably infinite rank: a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ corresponds to the fully invariant subgroup
$\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty)$ of all its laws, and $\mathfrak{U} \subseteq \mathfrak{V}$ if and only
if $\mathfrak{V}(F_\infty) \subseteq \mathfrak{U}(F_\infty)$. -/
abbrev GroupVarietyLattice : Type := (fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ))ᵒᵈ

/-- The least element of `GroupVarietyLattice` (the variety of trivial groups, whose laws form
all of `FreeGroup ℕ`) differs from its greatest element (the variety of all groups, whose only
law is trivial). -/
@[category test, AMS 6 8 20]
theorem GroupVarietyLattice.bot_ne_top : (⊥ : GroupVarietyLattice) ≠ ⊤ := by
  intro h
  have := congrArg (fun x : GroupVarietyLattice =>
    ((OrderDual.ofDual x : fullyInvariantSubgroup (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ))) h
  simp at this

/--
Does the lattice of all varieties of groups possess non-trivial automorphisms?

That is, is there an automorphism of the lattice of all varieties of groups (an order-preserving
bijection whose inverse is also order-preserving, equivalently a bijection preserving all meets
and joins) which is not the identity?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.27» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ φ : GroupVarietyLattice ≃o GroupVarietyLattice, φ ≠ OrderIso.refl _ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.27»

items: The lattice of all varieties of groups is not formalized as a class of groups (universe/class issues) but, following the decomposition notes, as the order dual of the lattice of fully invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ`, via the standard anti-isomorphism 𝔙 ↦ 𝔙(F_∞) (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups, Chapter 1). In `FreeGroup ℕ` fully invariant subgroups coincide with verbal subgroups, so this is exactly the lattice of varieties, with order reversed; the `ᵒᵈ` restores inclusion order of varieties. Since automorphisms of a lattice and of its dual are the same maps, the dual does not change the truth value but makes the type literally the lattice of varieties.

'Automorphism of the lattice' is taken to be an order automorphism (`OrderIso`), which for lattices coincides with lattice automorphism (bijection preserving ⊓ and ⊔, and in fact all sSup/sInf since the lattice is complete). 'Non-trivial' means different from the identity `OrderIso.refl _`.
Fully invariant is defined as `∀ f : G →* G, H.map f ≤ H` (mapped into itself by every endomorphism), mirroring Mathlib's `Submodule.IsFullyInvariant`.
AMS tags 6 (order/lattices), 8 (general algebraic systems, varieties) and 20 (group theory) were chosen.

reviewer_notes: The problem is a single yes/no question with no ambiguity of quantifiers. The only modelling choices are (a) how to represent 'the lattice of all varieties of groups' without a proper class, and (b) what 'non-trivial automorphism' means. For (a) the shipped file uses the classical fact (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups, Ch. 1) that 𝔙 ↦ 𝔙(F_∞) is an inclusion-reversing bijection between varieties and fully invariant subgroups of the free group of countably infinite rank; the file takes the order dual so the Lean type is order-isomorphic to the lattice of varieties under inclusion. For (b) an automorphism is an `OrderIso` L ≃o L (for lattices this coincides with bijections preserving ⊓ and ⊔, and indeed all sSup/sInf), and non-trivial means ≠ `OrderIso.refl`; I checked in Lean that this is equivalent to ∃ x, e x ≠ x and that the question is invariant under passing to the order dual. c04's alternative (varieties as S/H/P-closed classes of groups in `Type`) is also faithful (Birkhoff's theorem goes through inside `Type`, and its lattice is isomorphic to the one shipped), but was not chosen since the decomposition notes prefer the set-sized model and c04's faithfulness depends on a universe argument a reviewer must trust. c02/c06 put the carrier type in a `let` inside the theorem statement (stylistically poor); c05 uses a bare `Set` coerced to a type without proving it is a complete lattice; c03/c07 omit the order dual (harmless but less literal). No candidate omitted the slot.
